messages:
jess-cust: Hi team, we're suddenly getting 403s on our production calls to /v1/generate since ~16:20 UTC. Working token, same code. Response body: `{\"error\":\"permission_denied\",\"request_id\":\"req_9f7a2c\"}`

devon: Thanks — can you paste the exact curl you used (with token redacted) and the X-Request-Id from the response? Also which org/project is this under?

jess-cust: sure, here's sanitized curl (token = <REDACTED>):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v1","input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Response header excerpt: `x-request-id: req_9f7a2c`
Org header we set: `x-org-id: org-acme`

aj: quick guess — could be a scope/role change or a token that was re-issued for a project-scoped key. jess, can you run the same curl with `-v` and paste the full response headers (remove the token body)? Also include the last 6 chars of the token so we can match it against rotation logs.

jess-cust: pasted below, last 6 chars are `...a1b2c3`
--- response (redacted) ---
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< Date: Thu, 02 Mar 2025 16:20:12 GMT
< Content-Type: application/json
< Content-Length: 83
< x-request-id: req_9f7a2c
< x-rate-limit-remaining: 998
{"error":"permission_denied","message":"token missing required scope: inference.generate","request_id":"req_9f7a2c"}
--- end ---

sandeep: that error text is helpful — token lacks `inference.generate`. Two quick checks: 1) was the token issued as a project-scoped service key vs an org-scoped key? 2) did you recently rotate keys or change role mappings?

jess-cust: we rotated keys yesterday but I thought replacement was full-service. We used a script that swaps env var and restarts. No other config changed.

devon: ok, we'll correlate the token suffix `a1b2c3` against our rotation audit. Meanwhile can you run this exact repro and capture a debug bundle for us (it collects request/response and minimal env info) — run locally and upload the output. Command (replace token):
```
curl -s -D - -o /tmp/resp.json \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Org-Id: org-acme" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v1","input":"test"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
cat /tmp/resp.json; echo "--- headers saved ---"; env | grep -E 'TOKEN|ORG|PROJECT' | sed -E 's/(Bearer )?(.{4}).*(.{4})/\1****\2****\3/'
```
Please redact tokens before uploading to public threads. If you prefer, drop the bundle to S3 and DM a presigned link.

jess-cust: running now, will upload to your S3 share.

support-bot: Incident note created: INC-20250302-42, assigned to eng-support. Please include `req_9f7a2c` in the ticket.

aj: while we wait, devon/eng-support — check service logs for auth-policy changes at 16:15-16:25 UTC. Look specifically for policy `allow_inference_generate` and any rolebinding changes for org-acme.

devon: found audit entry — at 16:17 a service automation job removed `inference.generate` from a template applied to newly created project keys due to a mistaken config update. I can see the token suffix `a1b2c3` was issued at 16:05 and is project-scoped. That explains the 403s after rotation when the new env var pointed to a different token family.

sandeep: proposed fix: re-issue an org-scoped token or patch the project's rolebinding to include `inference.generate`. Which is easier for the customer?

jess-cust: reissue would be fastest for us. How quickly can you confirm issuer and revoke the broken key?

devon: we can revoke the broken key and issue a new org-scoped token. Before revocation, please run this command with the new token to validate (replace <NEW_TOKEN>):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <NEW_TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v1","input":"smoke"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
I'll also attach the matched audit log lines into INC-20250302-42.

jess-cust: got it. once you provision I'll test and report back. thanks! :pray:

devon: marking this thread for follow-up; if the new token still gets 403, include the full `x-request-id` header and the verbatim response body. Also note for engineering — automation runbook should fail-safe and not remove inference scopes from existing templates.

sandeep: adding a short postmortem checklist to the incident.

jess-cust: new token test successful, no 403s. closing on our side. thanks for the fast turnaround. :tada:
